records.title: Who is doing this, and on whose money
records.summary: Who runs Abilene
records.text: About this chapter | Abilene | ExposeTexas Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Abilene, TX of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → About · Abilene, TX Who is doing this, and on whose money This is the Abilene chapter of the Move Weight Foundation , a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. It is independent of the City of Abilene, of Taylor County, and of the State of Texas. It takes no money from any of them. How we source claims Every factual claim on this site links to a primary document or to a named outlet. Where a document exists, we publish the document rather than our description of it. We never invent a government phone number, address or docket number. Every contact datum is transcribed from an official published source and dated on the page. If we have not transcribed it yet, the page says so and links to the city's own directory instead of guessing. Every external link is fetched before it is published , and re-checked automatically every week. The result of that check is public on the automation page . Sources for this chapter were last verified 2026-07-26 . We publish released records whole. No redaction of a public record the government has already released. We never allege a crime. We publish the document, the amount and the date, and let readers and prosecutors do their own jobs. A submitter's identity is never published — not in a page, not in a filename, not in file metadata. We link out to local news and never republish it. What this chapter is not It is not a newspaper, not a campaign, and not aligned with any candidate, party or slate. It does not endorse. Its output is records, an archive, and the plain fact of whether a public body answered a lawful request on time. Funding The Foundation is funded by individual donations. Records cost money — Texas allows a body to charge for search and copying under § 552.2615, and a single large request can run into real numbers. Donations pay those invoices, the servers that hold the archive, and nothing else. Contributions are tax-deductible. Zelle: team@moveweight.com . Financial disclosures and the Form 990 are published by the Foundation at foundation.moveweight.com . Corrections If something here is wrong, we want to fix it and we will say that we did. Send the correction and, if you have it, the document — here . A correction is never quietly edited in; the change and its date stay on the page. Contact Records and requests: foia@moveweight.com Everything else: expose@moveweight.net

This page reports what actually happened, including when it failed. A site that quietly rots looks identical to one that is current, right up until somebody relies on it. So the status below is generated by the jobs themselves — it is not maintained by hand and cannot be made to look better than it is. Status Loading the last run… Job What it does Last run Result Detail Loading… What each job is allowed to do Agendas and meetings. Fetches only documents Abilene has already published, from CivicClerk at https://abilenetx.portal.civicclerk.com/ . It never logs in, never submits anything, and never touches a page the city has not made public. Link check. Re-fetches every external link this chapter publishes. Cities move pages, and a records-request link that 404s fails a reader at the exact moment they were about to act. Search index. Rebuilds the site's index from the pages and the extracted agenda text, so a resident can search a phrase and land on the agenda that carried it. Nothing writes to a government system. Records requests are sent by a person, deliberately, never by a timer. If a job has been red for a while That is a bug, not a policy. Tell us — the whole point of publishing this page is that somebody outside the project can see the failure before we do.

records.title: Every official link, in one place
records.summary: Verified links to Abilene city government, Taylor County offices, records portals, budgets and Texas oversight bodies. Checked 2026-07-26.
records.text: Abilene City Desk — every official link in one place | Abilene | ExposeTexas Skip to content Records & transparency Financial transparency https://www.abilenetx.gov/220/Financial-Transparency Form Center The City's online forms, including records requests. https://www.abilenetx.gov/FormCenter County & state Taylor County https://www.taylorcounty.texas.gov/ Texas AG — Open Government https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/open-government Texas oversight Where a Abilene decision gets reviewed by somebody who does not work for Abilene. Texas Attorney General — Open Government A body that wants to withhold must ask the AG within 10 business days. Those rulings are public and searchable, and they are the single best record of what a city tried to hide. Texas Comptroller — Transparency Local government debt, tax rates and economic-development agreements, filed by the entities themselves. Texas Open Data Portal Statewide datasets. Meetings, and how to be in the room Abilene publishes its agendas through CivicClerk : https://abilenetx.portal.civicclerk.com/ Agendas are posted ahead of the meeting because the law requires it. That posting is the single most useful document in local government and almost nobody opens it — it is where a contract award, a rate change or a tax abatement appears in public for the first time, usually as one line in a consent agenda. Reading a consent agenda Items on a consent agenda are voted through together, with no discussion, in a few seconds. That is not a trick — it is how a body gets through routine business. But it means the only chance to see an item is before the meeting, in the packet. Any member can pull an item out for discussion, and so can a resident who asks one in time. Where to watch → Open the agenda portal → A link that does not work Cities move pages. Every link on this page is re-checked automatically each week and the result is published on the automation page . If one is broken and we have not caught it, tell us .

records.title: The phases, the LLCs and the power plant
records.summary: Ten numbered companies, a generation plant, a 614-acre reinvestment zone and a year of closed-session items - all of it from Abilene
records.text: The phases, the LLCs and the power plant | Abilene | ExposeTexas Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Abilene, TX of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → Following the record · Abilene, TX The phases, the LLCs and the power plant Everything on this page comes from agendas the City of Abilene published itself. Every date links to the City’s own copy. Nothing here is an allegation — it is a reading list. What the agendas show Across 2025 and into 2026, Abilene City Council took up a data centre campus repeatedly — usually first in closed session under Texas Government Code § 551.087 , the business-prospect exception, and then in open session as votes on tax abatement agreements, site infrastructure agreements and zoning. The operator named throughout is Lancium . The counterparties are numbered companies: Abilene DC 1 and DC 3 through DC 10 , each tied to a numbered Phase . There is also Abilene DC TPP, LLC , which the City’s own agenda describes in parentheses as an Electricity Generation Plant . The single most specific item 4 December 2025, item 17. Tax abatement agreements and second tax abatement agreements with “Lancium LLC and Abilene DC 9, LLC (Phase 9), … Abilene DC 10, LLC (Phase 10), and Abilene DC TPP, LLC (Electricity Generation Plant).” The same meeting created Reinvestment Zone No. RZ25-1, approximately 614.91 acres . The sequence, with sources Date What the agenda says 23 Jan 2025 Item 14: approving collateral assignment of the Lancium, LLC and Abilene DC 1, LLC tax abatement agreements to JP Morgan Chase Bank . 13 Feb 2025 Amendments to the Amended and Restated tax abatement agreements with Lancium. 13 Mar 2025 Contract with BVNA for inspection services located at the Lancium Project . 11 Jun 2025 Closed session under § 551.087: “Project Diamond ( Crusoe & Lancium)”. 1 Jul 2025 Planning & Zoning: amending the buffer area of Planned Development District PDD-181 at 617 F.M. 2404 , legally described as the Lancium Addition , Taylor County. 28 Aug 2025 Item 28: tax abatement agreements and amended agreements with Lancium, LLC and Abilene DC 1, DC 3, DC 4, DC 5, DC 6, DC 7 and DC 8 . 3 Oct 2025 Closed session: “Lancium, Project Diamond”. 6 Nov 2025 Closed session: Project Surf, Project Rise, Lancium Project. Item 25: a Chapter 380 agreement for Project Surf. 20 Nov 2025 Closed session: Project Rainy Creek, Project Surf, Lancium Project. 4 Dec 2025 Item 17: Phase 9, Phase 10 and the Electricity Generation Plant abatements. Reinvestment Zone RZ25-1, ~614.91 acres. 8 Jan 2026 Closed session, then item 16 in open session: Site Infrastructure Agreements with Abilene DC9, LLC and Abilene DC10, LLC. What we notice, and what we do not claim Two things stand out on the face of the record, and neither is an accusation. There is a generation plant in the deal. A campus large enough to need its own electricity generation entity is a different proposition for a city than a warehouse, and it raises ordinary questions about power, water and who carries the cost of the connection. The agreements answer those questions. They are public records. The numbering skips two. The companies run DC 1 and DC 3 through DC 10, plus DC TPP. In the agendas indexed so far, DC 2 does not appear . That may mean nothing — entities get renamed, merged, or never formed — and we are not going to guess. It is noted because it is the kind of gap one request resolves in a line. We are not alleging that anything here was improper. Tax abatements, Chapter 380 agreements, reinvestment zones and § 551.087 closed sessions are ordinary, lawful instruments used by cities across Texas, and attracting investment is a legitimate thing for a council to do. The point is narrower: the negotiations happened in closed session and the resulting agreements are public. A resident is entitled to read what the City actually agreed to. The same tool, at two very different sizes Chapter 380 is worth understanding because Abilene uses it at both ends of the scale. The statute that appears beside these projects also appears in agreements with individual homebuilders under the City’s ReBuild ABI programme — single addresses on Peach Street and Minda Street. One instrument, a homebuilder at one end and a multi-company campus with its own power plant at the other. Reading both tells you more than reading either. What we are asking for The executed tax abatement agreements and second agreements named in the 28 August and 4 December 2025 items, in full, with all exhibits. The Site Infrastructure Agreements with Abilene DC9 and DC10 approved 8 January 2026. The ordinance and boundary description for Reinvestment Zone RZ25-1. Any water supply or utility service agreement referenced by those agreements, and the projected water demand relied on by the City. The certified agenda or tape of the § 551.087 sessions, which Texas requires a governmental body to keep. Requests are filed in the Move Weight Foundation’s name, so no resident has to attach their own to them. What comes back is published whole and unredacted here, alongside the City’s own copy. If you know something You do not have to identify yourself. Send documents or a pointer to abilene moveweight.net — a submitter’s identity is never published, in a page, a filename, or a file’s metadata. Sourced entirely from agendas published by the City of Abilene through its CivicClerk portal and re-indexed here every week. If any line on this page misreads a document, tell us and we will correct it and say that we did.

records.summary: A data centre campus with its own power plant, negotiated in closed session — a Move Weight Foundation chapter covering Abilene, Taylor County. File a records request, read the agendas, watch the meetings.
records.text: Abilene, TX — public records and meeting archive Skip to content Why Abilene Abilene's City Council has spent a year approving tax abatements, site infrastructure agreements and zoning for a data centre campus operated by Lancium, running through numbered companies - Abilene DC 1 and DC 3 to DC 10, each tied to a numbered phase - plus Abilene DC TPP, LLC, which the City's own agenda calls an Electricity Generation Plant. Most of it was discussed first under the business-prospect exception in Texas Government Code 551.087. That is lawful. It also means the negotiation happened in private and the agreements are the only public account of what was agreed. The Move Weight Foundation's first chapter is a town of thirteen thousand people in Ottawa County, Oklahoma, and it now holds 522 archived meetings with machine transcripts. The second is San Angelo, Texas. The third is Southaven, Mississippi, where the City's own released documents show an ad valorem agreement abating two thirds of property tax on a recital of twenty new jobs. None of those started with a tip. They started with somebody reading the agenda. If you already know something Send it anonymously . A submitter's identity is never published — not in a page, not in a filename, not in metadata.

records.title: Read the people who cover this every day
records.summary: Local and statewide newsrooms covering Abilene and Texas. We link out; we never republish another newsroom
records.text: Abilene news & allies | Abilene | ExposeTexas Skip to content Why we link instead of republish Local newsrooms are paid by attention. An aggregator that lifts a paragraph and keeps the reader on its own page takes that attention and gives nothing back, and then the newsroom shrinks and there is less reporting for everyone — including for us, because most of what a records request confirms was first noticed by a reporter. So the rule here is absolute: link out, never republish . The only documents hosted on this site are public records, which belong to the public already. Working on Abilene? If you are a reporter, a nonprofit or a resident group working on something here, the archive and the request pipeline are yours to use, and we will file on your behalf if a request under your own name would cost you something. Get in touch .

records.title: File a request the city has to answer
records.summary: How to file a public records request with the City of Abilene under Tex. Gov
records.text: File a Texas Public Information Act request in Abilene | Abilene | ExposeTexas Skip to content Build your letter This runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you type here is sent anywhere, stored, or seen by us — copy the result and send it yourself from your own email. Your name Your email What you are asking for Date range Ask for electronic delivery Require a cost estimate before charges Require an itemised legal basis for anything withheld Copy the letter Write the request narrow, then widen it “All emails about the project” gets refused as overbroad and burns your deadline. “Emails between the City Manager and [named party] between 1 March and 30 April” gets answered. Once you see what came back, ask again with what you learned. Two narrow requests beat one that never gets filled. Where to send it Abilene's own records channel is listed on the City Desk , with the exact URL the City publishes. Use it — a request filed through the body's own portal is the hardest one for it to say it never received. Send a copy to foia@moveweight.com at the same time. We log the send date, watch the deadline, and if it lapses we publish that fact. A request nobody knows about is a request the city can ignore quietly. Track the clock § 552.301 gives the City ten (10) business days. Put the send date in your calendar with that many days added, and put a second reminder a week later. Most requests are not denied — they are simply never answered, and the only thing that changes that is somebody noticing on the exact day. If you are refused Texas has no free citizen appeal board. If the City wants to withhold, it must ask the Attorney General for a ruling within ten business days (§ 552.301) and send you a copy of what it asked — that request and the ruling are both public, and they are the best record of what a city tried to hide. If the City simply never answers, a complaint goes to the county or district attorney under § 552.3215, or you can sue for mandamus under § 552.321. Keep the refusal Whatever the outcome, keep the exact wording of the denial and the date. A refusal that cites no statute, or cites one that does not apply, is itself the story — and it is the document an appeal turns on.

records.title: A data centre campus with its own power plant, negotiated in closed session
records.summary: The structural question this chapter was opened on, the specific public record that answers it, and what has been asked for so far.
records.text: What we are asking Abilene | Abilene | ExposeTexas Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Abilene, TX of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → The Question · Abilene, TX A data centre campus with its own power plant, negotiated in closed session Abilene's City Council has spent a year approving tax abatements, site infrastructure agreements and zoning for a data centre campus operated by Lancium, running through numbered companies - Abilene DC 1 and DC 3 to DC 10, each tied to a numbered phase - plus Abilene DC TPP, LLC, which the City's own agenda calls an Electricity Generation Plant. Most of it was discussed first under the business-prospect exception in Texas Government Code 551.087. That is lawful. It also means the negotiation happened in private and the agreements are the only public account of what was agreed. This is a question, not an accusation No one at this Foundation has alleged that anybody in Abilene has done anything wrong, and nothing on this site should be read that way. Chapters are opened on structural risk — large capital programmes, fast growth, a single dominant employer, a utility or authority that meets away from the council — because those are the conditions under which decisions get made with nobody watching. That is a statement about attention, not about anybody's conduct. Naming a city next to an accusation we have not documented would be precisely the thing this project exists to oppose. So the page you are reading names the question and the record that settles it, and then we go and ask for the record. The record that answers it The executed tax abatement agreements and second agreements with Lancium LLC and each Abilene DC entity, the Site Infrastructure Agreements approved 8 January 2026, the ordinance and boundary for Reinvestment Zone RZ25-1 (approximately 614.91 acres), and any water supply or utility service agreement they reference - all held by the City of Abilene. How this gets resolved Ask. A request goes to the City of Abilene under Tex. Gov't Code ch. 552. The City has ten (10) business days. Publish what comes back, whole. Released public records go up unredacted. We do not summarise a document in place of showing it, and we do not redact what the government already released. Publish what does not come back. A missed deadline, a refusal with no statute cited, an estimate that prices a resident out — those get published too, with dates. Silence is a finding. Rewrite this page. When the documents are in, this page stops being a question and becomes what the records showed — including if they showed nothing. A chapter that only ever reports wrongdoing is not doing arithmetic, it is doing marketing. What you can do right now You do not need us. The statute is yours, and a request from a resident of Abilene is harder to wave away than one from a nonprofit two states over. Build the letter → Where to send it → Send us something anonymously →

records.title: Watch your government
records.summary: Where to watch Abilene government on video — meeting recordings, agendas, and the archives that keep them after the city takes them down.
records.text: Watch your government | Abilene | ExposeTexas Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Abilene, TX of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → Video · Abilene, TX Watch your government Almost every decision that costs you money is made in a room with a camera in it. The recordings are public. Most people never find them because they are buried three clicks deep on a government site. Here they are. Where the video lives These are Abilene's own recordings and portals. We link to them rather than rehosting, so you are watching the authoritative copy. City of Abilene on YouTube City of Abilene The City's own channel, reached from abilenetx.gov/youtube. Open → We link, we do not rehost These are the government's own recordings on the government's own platforms. We send you there rather than mirroring them, so you are watching the authoritative copy and the view count lands where it belongs. The exception is when a recording disappears — see below. When a recording goes missing Meeting video gets taken down. Sometimes it is a retention policy, sometimes a platform migration, sometimes nobody can say why. Either way the public record evaporates, and the one meeting you needed is the one that is gone. That is why the Foundation's Miami, Oklahoma chapter keeps 522 meetings archived with machine transcripts and captions , mirrored to the Internet Archive. It is the deepest archive we run and the model for every other chapter. See what a full archive looks like → If you spot a gap A meeting with no video, a recording that ends mid-item, a link that used to work — tell us . A missing recording is itself a records request: the city holds the raw file whether or not it publishes it, and we will ask for it. Getting more out of a meeting recording Read the agenda packet first. It usually contains the actual contract or ordinance. The video is people discussing a document you can already have in front of you. Note the timestamp of anything that matters. A citation like "14 January, 1:42:10" is something a reporter or an auditor can verify in a minute. Watch the vote, not the speech. Who moved it, who seconded, who was absent, and whether it was on a published agenda. Executive session is a flag, not a crime. Bodies may close a meeting for defined reasons and must certify which. If a payment or a contract was discussed behind a closed door, the certification is a public record. Ask for it → Follow this chapter No social accounts yet for this chapter. We publish to the site first. Social accounts are a distribution channel, never the record — anything we post there exists here with its source document attached.

 In all cases, except where specifically stated otherwise, buildings must be secured and the lot clean and mowed by the 
owner within ten (10) days of receipt of notice of results of this hearing. If this is not done, the City may do so and bill the 
owner. In any case where the Board orders the owner to demolish a structure or structures, but the owner fails to demolish 
or appeal the Board's order, the City may demolish. Any appeal must be filed in district court within 30 calendar days after 
the aggrieved party receives notice of the Board's decision. At the hearing, you should be prepared to present the following

owner. In any case where the Board orders the owner to demolish a structure or structures, but the owner fails to demolish 
or appeal the Board's order, the City may demolish. Any appeal must be filed in district court within 30 calendar days after 
the aggrieved party receives notice of the Board's decision. At the hearing, you should be prepared to present the following

owner within ten (10) days of receipt of notice of results of this hearing. If this is not done, the City may do so and bill the 
owner. In any case where the Board orders the owner to demolish a structure or structures, but the owner fails to demolish 
or appeal the Board's order, the City may demolish. Any appeal must be filed in district court within 30 calendar days after 
the aggrieved party receives notice of the Board's decision. At the hearing, you should be prepared to present the following 
information: 
 1. Specific time frame needed to complete repairs.

owner within ten (10) days of receipt of notice of results of this hearing. If this is not done, the City may do so and bill the 
owner. In any case where the Board orders the owner to demolish a structure or structures, but the owner fails to demolish 
or appeal the Board's order, the City may demolish. Any appeal must be filed in district court within 30 calendar days after 
the aggrieved party receives notice of the Board's decision. At the hearing, you should be prepared to present the following

 1. Specific time frame needed to complete repairs.

All items listed in the Consent Agenda are considered routine by the City Council and will be enacted by 
one motion. There will be no separate discussion or presentation of these items unless otherwise 
requested by a Council Member. In the event one or more Council Members remove an item from the 
consent Agenda for separate discussion or presentation, the item or items removed will be considered in 
numerical order as part of the Regular Agenda and shall include a public hearing.

public comment period will be held. The public comment section of the consent agenda allows members 
of the public to present any ideas or information to the City Council and staff, and also allows for public 
comment on the consent agenda items not otherwise pulled for separate consideration. Neither the City 
Council nor staff will engage in discussion with the public during the public comments unless the item is 
listed on the Council agenda.

records.text:
1 
Board of Adjustment 
Meeting Minutes: May 13, 2025 

BOARD OF ADJUSTMENT REGULAR MEETING MINUTES 
May 13, 2025 
8:30 a.m. 

BOARD OF ADJUSTMENT OF THE CITY OF ABILENE, TEXAS 
CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS, 555 WALNUT STREET, ABILENE 
 
Members Present: 
Mr. Jon Loudermilk, Chair 
 
Ms. Shawnda Rixey, Vice Chair 
 
Mr. Louis Zientek, Secretary 
 
Ms. Melissa Sparks, Sergeant at Arms 

Mr. John Havard, Alternate 

Staff Present: 
Mr. Tim Littlejohn, Director 
 
Ms. Kelley Messer, First Assistant City Attorney 
 
Ms. Mason Teegardin, Planning Division Manager 
 
Ms. Kera Valois, Planner I 
 
Ms. Melissa Farr, Executive Assistant 

CALL TO ORDER 
 
The meeting was called to order at 8:30 a.m. and Ms. Melissa Farr recorded the minutes. A quorum 
was present, and the meeting proceeded. 

MINUTES 
 
The public hearing was opened. Seeing no one present and desiring to be heard, the public hearing 
was closed. Mr. Zientek made the motion to approve the minutes from the regular meeting held on 
March 11, 2025. Mr. Havard seconded the motion. The motion to approve the minutes prevailed 
by the following vote: 
 
AYES: Zientek, Rixey, Sparks, Havard, Loudermilk 
NAYS: None 
 
AGENDA ITEMS 
 
BA-2025-02: Receive a Report, Hold a Discussion and Public Hearing, and Take Action on a 
variance request by Nathan Franco. The subject property is located at 1758 Oldham Lane, Abilene, 
Texas. The variance request is to allow a 20’ rear setback, where a 25’ minimum is required. 

2 
Board of Adjustment 
Meeting Minutes: May 13, 2025 

Ms. Kera Valois presented this request. The subject property is currently zoned Planned 
Development (PDD-64) with a base zoning of Residential Single Family (RS-8). A permit was 
issued in November of 2023 for a single-family residence, with a minimum setback of 25 feet. The 
applicant informed us that he has built the home 5 additional feet into the 25’ minimum setback. 
This results in the applicant asking for a 20’ minimum setback. 
 
Mr. Loudermilk opened the public hearing. There were three individuals who stepped forward to 
speak. Seeing no one else present and desiring to speak, the public hearing was closed. 
 
Property owners within a 200-foot radius of the property address were notified. There were no (0) 
responses received in favor with one (1) received in opposition. 
 
Mr. Havard moved to approve the request based upon the lot size being a special circumstance. 
The motion is also made due to the existing hardship of rebuilding the structure not being caused 
by the petitioner because the error should have been caught during the building inspection. Mr. 
Zientek seconded the motion. The motion to approve prevailed by the following vote: 

AYES: Zientek, Rixey, Sparks, Havard, Loudermilk 
NAYS: None 
 
BA-2025-03: Receive a Report, Hold a Discussion and Public Hearing, and Take Action on a 
variance request by Kartavya (Kevin) Patel. The subject property is located at 1441 Barrow Street, 
Abilene, Texas. The request for the variance is to allow one (1) parking space, where ten (10) are 
required. 
 
Ms. Kera Valois presented this request. The subject property is zoned General Commercial (GC) 
and is being proposed for a new development. The current use of the lot is a pizza restaurant, and 
the applicant is proposing to demolish and build a 7 Brew. Once an existing building is demolished, 
any new development is required to conform to the standards set out in the Land Development 
Code. The proposed 7 Brew is currently in the Site Plan review phase, where a parking issue has 
been identified. Drive-thru restaurants are required to have a minimum of ten (10) parking spaces, 
no matter the building square footage. 
 
Mr. Loudermilk opened the public hearing. Seeing no one present and desiring to be heard, the 
public hearing was closed. 
 
Property owners within a 200-foot radius of the property address were notified. There were no (0) 
responses received in favor nor in opposition. 
 
Ms. Rixey moved to deny the request. Ms. Sparks seconded the motion. The motion to deny 
prevailed by the following vote: 
 
AYES: Zientek, Rixey, Sparks, Havard, Loudermilk 
NAYS: None 

3 
Board of Adjustment 
Meeting Minutes: May 13, 2025 

ADJOURNMENT 
 
There being no further business, Mr. Zientek moved to adjourn. Ms. Rixey seconded the motion. 
The meeting was adjourned at 8:58 a.m. 

Approved: ______________________________, Chair 

Jon Loudermilk 
Jon Loudermilk (Jun 10, 2025 13:46 CDT)

meeting to deliberate the purchase, exchange, lease or value of real property if 
deliberation in an open meeting would have a detrimental effect on the position of the 
governmental body in negotiations with a third person. And, Section 551.073 allows a 
governmental body to deliberate a negotiated contract for a prospective gift or donation 
to the governmental body if deliberation in a open meeting would have a detrimental 
effect on the position of the governmental body in negotiations with a third person. 
Additionally, Section 551.087 allows a governmental body to discuss or deliberate on 
commercial or financial information that has been received from a business prospect 
that the governmental body seeks to have locate, stay, or expand in or near the City and 
with which there may be ongoing negotiations or deliberate the offer of a financial or 
other incentive to a business prospect. Further, Section 551.071 provides that a 
governmental body may seek advice from its attorney regarding a pending or 
contemplated litigation subject, settlement offer, or attorney-client privileged 
information. After discussion in executive session, any action or vote will be taken in 
public.

 STATEMENT OF POLICY 
 In all cases, except where specifically stated otherwise, buildings must be secured and the lot clean and mowed by the 
owner within ten (10) days of receipt of notice of results of this hearing. If this is not done, the City may do so and bill the 
owner. In any case where the Board orders the owner to demolish a structure or structures, but the owner fails to demolish 
or appeal the Board's order, the City may demolish. Any appeal must be filed in district court within 30 calendar days after 
the aggrieved party receives notice of the Board's decision. At the hearing, you should be prepared to present the following 
information:

owner within ten (10) days of receipt of notice of results of this hearing. If this is not done, the City may do so and bill the 
owner. In any case where the Board orders the owner to demolish a structure or structures, but the owner fails to demolish 
or appeal the Board's order, the City may demolish. Any appeal must be filed in district court within 30 calendar days after 
the aggrieved party receives notice of the Board's decision. At the hearing, you should be prepared to present the following 
information: 
 1. Specific time frame needed to complete repairs.

Child Advocacy Board 
Special Called Meeting Minutes 
3/4/2025 

Attendance: Casey Wasson, Jim Hicks, Brandon Gerganus, Phil Crowley, Maggie 
Brennan, Kerri Barber, Misti Coller, Angie Cross, Craig Shaw, Heather Hadlock, Alana 
Jeter, Jeff Cook, Tim Bundick, Kari Leong, Nikki Hill 
 
Call to Order at 1614 
1. Public comment on any item on the agenda 
a. Discussion of possible changes to by-laws 
i. Decrease quorum to 1/3 of membership 
ii. Amend Ex Officio requirement which currently prevents Phil 
Crowley from continuing position as board Chair 
b. Will allow board members time to review by-laws and make any additional 
amendment changes to board officers (Phil, Misti, Casey and Craig) by 
March 25, 2025 
c. By-law amendment changes will be discussed and voted on during 
meeting 5/9/2025 
2. Approval of minutes from 2/10/2025 meeting 
a. Motion: Jim Hicks 
b. Second: Phil Crowley 
c. Motion passed 
Agenda Items 
3. Welcome/Introductions – New Board Member Tim Bundick 
a. Board introductions made 
b. Tim joins us as the current Director of Security at McMurry University 
4. Loose Change for Change Event 
a. PrimeTime: 5/9/2025 date available and to be set for event so schools can 
be notified 
b. $11 per child which would include one game of bowling and 2 slices of 
pizza per child 
c. Craig will reach out about adding $5 arcade card, utilize sponsorship 
funds if needed in order to provide additional rewards to the students 

d. Board determined that we will request students not bring any additional 
money for games/snacks to prevent inequality. We will also request 
parents not attend event. 
e. Discussed changing the day of the week that the event is held for 2026 so 
that Merkel elementary can participate (Merkel has 4 day school week) 
5. Discussion and Update 
a. Removal of DEI in accordance with executive order – literature changes 
have been made on state and local level. No changes will be made in care 
provided and center will remain culturally sensitive. Demographic gaps will 
continue to be taken into consideration 
b. Overview of community assessment conducted by CAC 
6. Director’s Update 
a. Bi-Annual visit overview & introduction of inspectors in attendance – 
Present at meeting. Visit underway to evaluate if local CAC is meeting 
state standards. 
b. Status of Funding Outlook – VOCA funding has decreased 67% since 
2018 and sustainability concerns have been raised. Bill HR 909 redirects 
funds to sustain VOCA funds 
c. Overview of hiring process to be used to find next CAC Director – Will

 STATEMENT OF POLICY 
 In all cases, except where specifically stated otherwise, buildings must be secured and the lot clean and mowed by the 
owner within ten (10) days of receipt of notice of results of this hearing. If this is not done, the City may do so and bill the 
owner. In any case where the Board orders the owner to demolish a structure or structures, but the owner fails to demolish 
or appeal the Board's order, the City may demolish. Any appeal must be filed in district court within 30 calendar days after 
the aggrieved party receives notice of the Board's decision. At the hearing, you should be prepared to present the following 
information: 
 1. Specific time frame needed to complete repairs. 
 2. Specific scope of repair work to be completed. 
 3. Cost estimates for work to be done by licensed, bonded contractors such as electrical, plumbing or heating and 
 air-conditioning contractors. 
 
 You have the right to hire an attorney to represent you at the hearing, the right to inspect the file on the property at the

records.text:
Child Advocacy Board Minutes 
January 7, 2025 

Attendance: Amy Bailey, Alana Jeter, Angie Cross, Aubri Ward, Maggie Brennan, 
Craig Shaw, Kerri Barber, Heather Hadlock, Jason Shaw, Jim Hicks, Kari Leong, Karn 
Bingaman-Hall, Misti Collier, Phil Crowley 
 
Call to Order at 4:00p.m. by Jason Shaw 
1. Public comment on any item on the agenda – No public comment was given. 
2. Approve minutes from 11/5/2024 board meeting 
a. Motion by Misti Collier 
b. 2nd by K Bingaman-Hall 
c. Motion passed, minutes approved as presented 
3. Discussion and Possible Action: Nominations and Voting for Board Positions.: A 
discussion was held and Phil Crowley was nominated as Chair, Misti Collier was 
nominated as Vice-Chair, Craig Shaw was nominated as Treasurer, and Casey 
Wasson was nominated as Secretary for one year terms. 
a. Jim Hicks made the motion to create the slate of candidates 
b. seconded by Aubri Ward. 
c. This motion passed unanimously. 
d. Jim Hicks made the motion to elect the slate of Officers 
e. seconded by Karon Bingaman Hall. 
f. This motion passed unanimously. 
 
4. Speaker: John Graham from Taylor County Sheriffs Office -Best Practices for Child 
Advocacy Centers: Taylor County Sheriff Detective John Graham presented ideas 
about possible Abilene Child Advocacy Center future programs and a discussion was 
held. No action was taken. 
 
5. Discussion and Possible Action: Loose Change for Change 
a. Change for Change Bank Account: A discussion was held to remove Melinda 
Beard from the First Financial bank account and place Amy Bailey on the bank 
account, on the signature card, and place Amy Bailey on any other documents 
that First Financial Bank requires or recommends and this motion was 
seconded by Jim Hicks. This motion passed unanimously. 
b. Karon Bingaman Hall made a motion to keep the First Financial bank account 
as is with any necessary name changes and this was seconded by Craig 
Shaw. This motion passed unanimously. 

c. Winners for Loose Change for Change: A discussion was held for possible 
dates and event centers to hold a party for the Winners for Loose Change 
Challenge. No action was taken. 
 
6. Division Manager's Report 
c. Grant Updates discussion was held and no action was taken. 
d. Discussion and Possible Action: Recommendations for Board Trainings in 
2025- A discussion was held and no action was taken. 
e. Discussion and Possible Action: Fiscal Year 2025 Strategic Plan- A 
discussion was held and Phil Crowley made a motion to approve the proposed 
Fiscal Year 2025 Strategic Plan and this was seconded by Jim Hicks. This 
motion passed unanimously 

5:22 p.m. Meeting Adjourned – Next meeting will be March 4, 2025 at 4:00 pm.
